MKTG 350.description: Principles and concepts underlying marketing functions, including the conception, pricing, promotion, and distribution of products and services and the role of marketing in society.
MKTG 350.subject: MKTG
MKTG 350.title: Principles of Marketing

MKTG 351.description: The consumer decision process, with emphasis on consumer decision making, satisfaction/dissatisfaction factors, perception, learning, group influences, and marketing strategy implications.
MKTG 351.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 351.subject: MKTG
MKTG 351.title: Consumer Behavior

MKTG 352.description: Investigates the theory and practice of marketing research with emphasis on the problem-oriented nature of marketing research and how research activities are implemented by marketing researchers and used by managers.
MKTG 352.subject: MKTG
MKTG 352.title: Principles of Marketing Research

MKTG 445.description: Understand the fundamentals of the sales process and how to ensure client engagement. Learn follow-up skills that will help you in every walk of life. Learn the fundamentals of effective business communication (voicemail, email, and hand-written).
MKTG 445.subject: MKTG
MKTG 445.title: Sales Strategy

MKTG 446.description: The context, tools and conceptual understanding of the technology-related and managerial expectations of an entry level sales representative.
MKTG 446.subject: MKTG
MKTG 446.title: Sales Automation and Customer Management

MKTG 447.description: An in-depth understanding of the fundamentals of pricing strategy formulation and implementation.
MKTG 447.subject: MKTG
MKTG 447.title: Pricing Strategy and Analytics

MKTG 448.description: The conceptual, applied, and managerial elements of advanced data science methods for business decision-making.
MKTG 448.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B+ or better in MGSC 291.
MKTG 448.subject: MKTG
MKTG 448.title: Data Science for Business Decision-Making

MKTG 451.description: Reading and research on selected topics in marketing. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
MKTG 451.subject: MKTG
MKTG 451.title: Topics in Marketing

MKTG 452.description: In this course students will learn about how to sell various products/services. The concepts will be brought to life with real tools and training from several companies. This “Experiential Learning” class involves learning by participating in real professional sales in action.
MKTG 452.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350, MKTG 352, MKTG 457.
MKTG 452.subject: MKTG
MKTG 452.title: Sales Practicum

MKTG 453.description: Students form a working marketing agency and complete a real-world marketing campaign for a client. Working as a team, they apply marketing theory and concepts to a substantively important marketing problem.
MKTG 453.subject: MKTG
MKTG 453.title: Marketing Practicum

MKTG 454.description: Marketing strategy in marketing to other business and nonprofit organizations, emphasizing relationship building, alliances and partnerships, data interchange, power shifts in the channel and the impact of changing technology.
MKTG 454.subject: MKTG
MKTG 454.title: Business-to-Business Marketing

MKTG 455.description: Integration of advertising, sales promotion, point-of-purchase communications toward the goal of enhancing brand equity.
MKTG 455.subject: MKTG
MKTG 455.title: Marketing Communications and Strategy

MKTG 456.description: The Sales Management course is the study of building and leading high-performance sales teams to grow revenue for organizations.
MKTG 456.subject: MKTG
MKTG 456.title: Sales Management

MKTG 457.description: Examines fundamentals of personal selling and sales management and the development of communication and selling skills that yield desired sales results.
MKTG 457.subject: MKTG
MKTG 457.title: Introduction To Sales

MKTG 459.description: Marketing functions and channel flows used to develop distribution strategies that provide effective, efficient, and reliable delivery of products and services to end-user markets.
MKTG 459.subject: MKTG
MKTG 459.title: Marketing Channels and Distribution

MKTG 460.description: The primary tasks involved in developing marketing strategies from a product and/or brand management perspective, including product policy, competitive analysis, pricing, brand equity management, marketing information systems management, sales forecasting and monitoring customer satisfaction.
MKTG 460.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 460.subject: MKTG
MKTG 460.title: Product and Brand Management

MKTG 461.description: Studies retail institutions, relationships with other channel members, factors influencing patronage patterns, adapting to change in dynamic environments with emphasis on strategy implications for managers in retail organizations.
MKTG 461.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 461.subject: MKTG
MKTG 461.title: Retailing Management

MKTG 465.description: Management of marketing organizations and integration of functions, with emphasis on planning and designing strategies and applying tools and techniques for problem solving and decision making. For marketing majors only.
MKTG 465.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350 and MKTG 352.
MKTG 465.subject: MKTG
MKTG 465.title: Marketing Strategy and Planning

MKTG 468.description: The development of new products (products or services) is a cross-functional process inside any organization. This course explores this process and how new product development managers are responsible for leading an organization from identifying marketing opportunities or gaps through product commercialization. This course is focused on how companies take ideas, prioritizes them and ultimately makes them a reality.
MKTG 468.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 468.subject: MKTG
MKTG 468.title: New Product Development

MKTG 470.description: This course aims to prepare students to be effective leaders in marketing analytics, especially in the dynamic context of digital platforms and social media.
MKTG 470.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 470.subject: MKTG
MKTG 470.title: Digital Marketing Social Media Analytics

MKTG 472.description: Sustainability (environmental, social, and economic performance) is a top priority for CEOs and is increasingly embedded into business strategy, resulting in changing business models, product strategies and innovation, etc. This course explores the challenges and opportunities facing businesses through a sustainability lens. Through readings, speakers, discussions and critical thinking exercises, students will gain exposure to the key environmental and social issues facing businesses today and how they are reacting. Emphasis will be placed on understanding the tradeoffs between economic, environmental and social performance. Throughout the semester, students will analyze the complex tradeoffs and leverage various frameworks to understand how businesses determine their strategic priorities, measure performance, and communicate that to key stakeholders.
MKTG 472.subject: MKTG
MKTG 472.title: Business, Markets and Sustainability

MKTG 475.description: Understand and demonstrate benefit and solution-based sales processes. Create daily discipline to drive sales performance.
MKTG 475.subject: MKTG
MKTG 475.title: Consultative Selling with Certification

MKTG 477.description: An introduction to Marketing on the predominant social media platforms (e.g. Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, etc).
MKTG 477.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 477.subject: MKTG
MKTG 477.title: Social Media Marketing

MKTG 479.description: Overview of the unique challenges associated with marketing the offerings of a nonprofit organization. Organizing, planning, implementing, and controlling marketing efforts of nonprofit organizations. Focus on fundraising, market research, positioning, and communications.
MKTG 479.subject: MKTG
MKTG 479.title: Marketing for Nonprofit Organizations

MKTG 498.description: Student will participate in a Sales Internship for the duration of the current semester. The scope of the work for the internship must be agreed upon by the student, a representative of the DMBS undergrad advisement office, the professor and the internship coordinator for the company before the semester starts.
MKTG 498.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 498.subject: MKTG
MKTG 498.title: Sales Internship

MKTG 499.description: Student will participate in a Marketing Internship for the duration of the current semester. The scope of the work for the internship must be agreed upon by the student, a representative of the DMBS undergrad advisement office, the professor and the internship coordinator for the company before the semester starts.
MKTG 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 350.
MKTG 499.subject: MKTG
MKTG 499.title: Marketing Internship

MKTG 701.description: Marketing function with emphasis on the procedures and techniques for analyzing, planning, and implementing marketing strategies and tactics related to product, pricing, communication, and distribution decisions.
MKTG 701.subject: MKTG
MKTG 701.title: Marketing Management

MKTG 702.description: Research methodology as applied to marketing problems; includes research problem definition, sample design, data collection procedures, valid and reliable measurement, data analysis techniques, and sales forecasting fundamentals.
MKTG 702.subject: MKTG
MKTG 702.title: Marketing Research

MKTG 703.description: Tools and techniques for creating marketing plans.
MKTG 703.subject: MKTG
MKTG 703.title: Marketing Planning

MKTG 704.description: Concepts, theories, and techniques applicable to obtaining a sophisticated understanding of consumer motives, attitudes, decision-making processes, and satisfaction determinants.
MKTG 704.subject: MKTG
MKTG 704.title: Consumer Behavior

MKTG 705.description: Advertising, sales promotions, marketing-oriented public relations, event and sponsorship marketing, point-of-purchase communications, and other aspects of integrated marketing communications.
MKTG 705.subject: MKTG
MKTG 705.title: Marketing Communications

MKTG 706.description: The role and activities of sales in marketing, including concepts, practices, and procedures of sales force management.
MKTG 706.subject: MKTG
MKTG 706.title: Sales and Sales Management

MKTG 707.description: Product line and portfolio planning, stage-gate approach to new product development, product launch and product life cycle management, and branding strategies and procedures.
MKTG 707.subject: MKTG
MKTG 707.title: Product and Branding Policies

MKTG 708.description: Techniques, procedures, and software applications for database marketing, managing customer relations, and mining large databases.
MKTG 708.subject: MKTG
MKTG 708.title: Customer Relationship Management and Data Mining

MKTG 709.description: The Internet as both a marketing channel and communication medium, including E-commerce from a marketing perspective.
MKTG 709.subject: MKTG
MKTG 709.title: Internet Marketing

MKTG 710.description: An integrative treatment of the role of marketing in strategic problem solving.
MKTG 710.subject: MKTG
MKTG 710.title: Strategic Marketing

MKTG 711.description: This course explores sustainability through a marketing lens. Emphasis is placed on understanding the tradeoffs between economic, environmental and social performance while making product, price, distribution and promotional decisions.
MKTG 711.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 701 or DMSB 716.
MKTG 711.subject: MKTG
MKTG 711.title: Business, Markets, and Sustainability

MKTG 712.description: Readings and research on selected topics in marketing. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
MKTG 712.subject: MKTG
MKTG 712.title: Topics in Marketing Thought and Practice

MKTG 713.description: This course explores the importance of customer satisfaction in today's marketplace and the challenges of designing and implementing an actual customer satisfaction measurement process.
MKTG 713.subject: MKTG
MKTG 713.title: Managing Customer Satisfaction

MKTG 715.description: Economics and behavioral foundations of pricing strategy formulation and implementation.
MKTG 715.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MKTG 701 or DMSB 701 or equivalent.
MKTG 715.subject: MKTG
MKTG 715.title: Pricing Strategy and Analysis

MKTG 716.description: Building competencies that help managers acquire knowledge from clients and apply it in ways that enhance openness in building strategic responses.
MKTG 716.subject: MKTG
MKTG 716.title: Listening to the Voice of the Market

MKTG 717.description: The critical thinking, statistical tools, and marketing application of business analytics.
MKTG 717.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: DMSB 716 or MKTG 701 and DMSB 712 or MGSC 711.
MKTG 717.subject: MKTG
MKTG 717.title: Fundamentals of Marketing Analytics

MKTG 718.description: Develop a social and digital media plan/solution to present to a client. Business enterprises and even non-business organizations are demanding new marketing hires and their marketing agencies have an acute understanding of how to develop and utilize online and social media as part of their integrated marketing plans. Both business-to-consumer and business-to-business enterprises are migrating to social media as a primary form of communication with customers and partners.
MKTG 718.subject: MKTG
MKTG 718.title: Social and Digital Media Strategies for Businesses

MKTG 719.description: Identifying, developing, communicating and commercializing a value proposition between businesses in the form of a product or service.
MKTG 719.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in DMSB 716 or MKTG 701.
MKTG 719.subject: MKTG
MKTG 719.title: Business to Business Marketing

MKTG 720.description: Examines and explores the Sales function within the modern organization. In addition to addressing the practical and classic sales issues of alignment, structure, performance and development, the course will also review the technologies and trends that are changing the commercial landscape and causing the fast evolution of the sales function.
MKTG 720.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in DMSB 716 or MKTG 701.
MKTG 720.subject: MKTG
MKTG 720.title: Sales: Process, People and Performance

MKTG 722.description: The conceptual, applied, and managerial elements of machine learning for business decision-making.
MKTG 722.subject: MKTG
MKTG 722.title: Machine Learning for Business Decision Making

MKTG 723.description: Analytical techniques for generating insights in marketing areas such as customer analytics, product analytics, marketing-mix analytics and social media analytics.
MKTG 723.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 701 or DMSB 716; C or better in MGSC 711.
MKTG 723.subject: MKTG
MKTG 723.title: Marketing Analytics

MKTG 725.description: This course explores the transformative impact of AI on marketing, equipping students with the knowledge and skills to leverage AI tools in real-world marketing scenarios. Through a combination of theoretical insights, practical applications, and critical analysis, students will learn how to use AI to enhance market analysis, target audience definition, brand development, and go-to-market strategies.
MKTG 725.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 701 or DMSB 716.
MKTG 725.subject: MKTG
MKTG 725.title: AI in Marketing

MKTG 726.description: Non-profit organizations are important constituents in today’s business world, and their marketing efforts face unique issues and challenges that are different from for-profit organizations. Through lectures, cases, discussions, and a project, this course will examine what is unique about doing marketing in certain nonprofit sectors (e.g., arts, religious, social welfare, associations, charities, universities, hospitals, and government agencies). Students will come away from the course with an improved ability to organize, plan, implement, and control the marketing efforts of nonprofit organizations. It will also focus on certain marketing tasks that are crucial for nonprofit managers (e.g., fundraising, doing marketing research, positioning, and communications).
MKTG 726.subject: MKTG
MKTG 726.title: Marketing for Nonprofit Organizations

MKTG 740.description: This course aims to prepare students to be effective leaders in marketing analytics, especially in the dynamic context of digital platforms and social media.
MKTG 740.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MKTG 701 or DMSB 716 or equivalent.
MKTG 740.subject: MKTG
MKTG 740.title: Digital Marketing Social Media Analytics

MKTG 744.description: Management concepts, methods, and frameworks to conceive, support, deploy, evaluate, and safeguard data science and AI initiatives.
MKTG 744.subject: MKTG
MKTG 744.title: Managing Artificial Intelligence and Data Science

MKTG 750.description: Develop successful marketing strategies using data, research, and analysis to create impactful strategies for real business clients. Businesses and recruiters are increasingly demanding experience handling practical problems faced by a marketing manager from our MBA students. In this elective course, the students get that experience.
MKTG 750.subject: MKTG
MKTG 750.title: Marketing Consulting Project

MKTG 850.description: Doctoral seminar covering research methods and philosophies that underpin knowledge generation in marketing.
MKTG 850.subject: MKTG
MKTG 850.title: Research Methods and Philosophies in Marketing

MKTG 851.description: Doctoral seminar exploring concepts, theories, and research methods relevant to understanding consumer behavior.
MKTG 851.subject: MKTG
MKTG 851.title: Concepts and Theories in Consumer Research

MKTG 852.description: Doctoral seminar involving intensive study and criticism of the current consumer research literature.
MKTG 852.subject: MKTG
MKTG 852.title: Current Topics in Consumer Research

MKTG 853.description: Doctoral seminar investigating contemporary analytic techniques for testing marketing theories.
MKTG 853.subject: MKTG
MKTG 853.title: Analytic Techniques for Marketing Decision Making

MKTG 854.description: Doctoral seminar examining covariance structure methods for developing measures of unobservable constructs and testing structural models.
MKTG 854.subject: MKTG
MKTG 854.title: Latent Variable Estimation Techniques

MKTG 855.description: A directed project for marketing Ph.D. students requiring literature synthesis of a selected topical area and formulation of original concepts and theoretical propositions.
MKTG 855.subject: MKTG
MKTG 855.title: Conceptualization in Marketing

MKTG 856.description: A directed project for marketing Ph.D. students requiring an empirical investigation and testing of theoretical propositions.
MKTG 856.subject: MKTG
MKTG 856.title: Empirical Testing of Theoretical Propositions in Marketing

MKTG 857.description: Doctoral seminar covering advances in marketing science models, including brand choice, product development, media choice, and other models.
MKTG 857.subject: MKTG
MKTG 857.title: Marketing Models

MKTG 858.description: Doctoral seminar investigating emerging paradigms and theory regarding the role of marketing within the firm and the effects of marketing mix variables on consumer behavior and firm performance.
MKTG 858.subject: MKTG
MKTG 858.title: Seminar in Marketing Strategy I

MKTG 860.description: The course aims to provide good understanding of endogeneity issues in marketing strategy research and the empirical strategies that one can adopt to credibly estimate the effects of interest. The students should have a graduate level understanding of econometrics to benefit from this course.
MKTG 860.subject: MKTG
MKTG 860.title: Empirical Causal Analyses for Marketing Strategy Research
